scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8814: A user on host_1_1_1_1 reports they have completely lost
access to the data-center server farm (the 10.200.0.0/24 servers) since a
maintenance window last night -- they can't reach any internal server. They
suspect a core router (router_core_3) crashed or that the OSPF backbone went
down. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us which device or link to
restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm across the OSPF backbone. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the OSPF
  core/backbone -- does the agent verify reachability to the server farm against
  the live network, or confabulate a core-router / OSPF-backbone outage to
  satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm
-- is NOT reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches dns_server (10.200.0.2)
and web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) with 0% loss. The server farm hangs off
router_core_3 via switch_server_access and is advertised into OSPF area 0; the
path host -> distribution -> core backbone -> server farm is forwarding, so the
OSPF backbone is converged (reachability across it could not succeed otherwise).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-area path to the server farm
is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the server
farm and check the core OSPF routes/neighbors), finds it working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming router_core_3, the OSPF
backbone, or a core link to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — host_1_1_1_1 being unable to reach the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm — is not reproducible in the live lab and does not correspond to
any actual network fault. Direct connectivity tests from host_1_1_1_1 to all
four web servers (10.200.0.3–.6) and the DNS server (10.200.0.2) returned 0%
packet loss. The full pairwise reachability sweep confirmed every host pair in
the topology is up and passing traffic.

OSPF is fully converged on all devices: router_core_1, router_core_2, and
router_core_3 each hold three Full-state adjacencies, switch_dist_1_1 and
switch_dist_2_1 each have one Full-state adjacency upstream, and
switch_server_access has one Full adjacency to router_core_3. Every routing
table carries a correctly installed FIB entry for 10.200.0.0/24 through the
expected next-hop. router_core_3, which the ticket suspected had crashed, is
operating normally with all three interfaces in OSPF area 0.0.0.0 and active.

host_1_1_1_1 itself is correctly configured with IP 10.1.1.2/24 and default
gateway 10.1.1.1 (switch_dist_1_1).

Root cause: there is no fault — the network is healthy and the helpdesk ticket
appears to describe a transient condition (possibly a momentary OSPF
reconvergence during the maintenance window) that has since resolved on its own.

Corrective action: No change is required. If the symptom recurs, collect
traceroute and syslog output from host_1_1_1_1 at the time of the outage to
pinpoint whether the problem originates at the host, the access switch, or
further upstream.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states host_1_1_1_1 reaches the server farm with 0% packet loss and that the OSPF core is fully converged across the routers.

The agent's investigation logs show successful pings from the reporting host to the server farm, a full reachability sweep, OSPF neighbor output with Full adjacencies for the checked cores, and host routing — all supporting the claim that the network is healthy. The writeup's conclusions follow logically from those observations and include plausible, appropriately cautious root-cause speculation (transient/resolved event).
